preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is an integer between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.
The number of extra edges m is an integer between 0 and 4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(extra_edges) == m and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in extra_edges)
preconditions.description: There are exactly m extra edges, each connecting two distinct nodes u and v within the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: tree_edges == [(i, i // 2) for i in range(2, n + 1)]
preconditions.description: The base graph is a complete binary tree where the parent of node i (for i >= 2) is floor(i/2).

postconditions.description: The output is the count of all simple paths in the graph formed by the tree edges and extra edges, modulo 10^9 + 7. A simple path is a sequence of distinct nodes where consecutive nodes are connected by an edge (tree or extra), including single-node paths.
